correctness.rationale: For all nonzero complex a with 0<\(q=|a|^2\)<1 and |tau|=(1-q)/2, the exact Gaussian kernel of \(W^*W\) has A=q/D and B=tau conjugate(a)²/D, D=1-4|tau|²=q(2-q). A Fock rotation makes B negative, matching exactly the Bargmann kernel of multiplication by q^(-1/2)exp(-(1-q)x²). Dense reproducing-kernel spans establish bounded extension. Multiplication-spectrum theory proves pure twofold absolutely continuous spectrum, exact norm and essential norm. The explicit power identity and Hilbert-Schmidt Gaussian integral prove \(W^2\) compact for nonreal a, and the Taylor eigenvalue equation yields only \(a^n\); for real a each W^n again lies on the same boundary, yielding exact norm \(q^{-n/4}\) and no point eigenvalues. The compact subcritical approximation satisfies strong dominated convergence and constant essential-norm separation. The standalone verification program passed 169 finite supplementary checks; those checks are not used as infinite proofs.
